title: What seven years at Airbnb taught Lenny about building a business: culture, focus, ambitious goals
summary: Lenny distills seven years at Airbnb into lessons on culture, problem statements, wildly ambitious goals, working backward from the ideal experience, org design, a high bar, and team focus. Practical, with concrete Airbnb examples like Instant Book and Snow White.

principles.text: A well-crafted, aligned problem statement is the single most important step in solving any problem.
principles.quote: Crafting and aligning on a problem statement is the single most important step in solving any problem.

principles.text: Set uncomfortable goals and give each one a single accountable owner by name.
principles.quote: If a number doesn’t have a person’s name next to it, it’s not going to happen.

principles.text: Start from the ideal user experience and work backward instead of micro-optimizing the funnel.
principles.quote: Instead of spending months or years micro-optimizing individual parts of the funnel, we stepped back and explored what the ideal booking experience would look like.

principles.text: Treat org design as a product: dedicated cross-functional teams with a clear mandate, few dependencies.
principles.quote: Optimize for dedicated cross-functional teams with a clear mandate.

principles.text: Good goals are few, fast-feedback, tied to top-line growth, easy to understand, and uncomfortable.
principles.quote: Goals should 1) be limited in number — ideally just one or two, 2) have quick feedback loops that allow you to see impact immediately, 3) be directly connected to top-line business growth, 4) be easily understood, and 5) be uncomfortable.

principles.text: Hire only people you feel strongly about; a maybe is a no.
principles.quote: My advice is to only hire people you feel “hell yes” about. If it’s a maybe, it’s a no.
